chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Uqba ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'We visit the mosques around Medina, so which of them should I begin with?' He said: 'Begin with Quba, so pray in it and frequent it, for it is the first mosque in this earth wherein the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed.'
Then go to the drinking place of Umm Ibrahim, so pray in it, and it is the dwelling of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and his place of prayer.
Then you go to the mosque of Al-Fadikh, so pray in it, for your Prophet had prayed in it.
When you have fulfilled this side, you go to the side of Uhud, so begin with the mosque which is near the Harrah, so pray in it.
Then you pass by the grave of Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, and greet upon him.
Then you pass by the graves of the martyrs, so stand by them and say: 'Peace be upon you, O people of the houses! You have preceded us and we are following you.'
Then you go to the mosque which was in the open space beside the mountain, on your right when you enter Uhud, so pray in it.
For there the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) went out to Uhud when he met the Polytheists. They did not move away until the time for prayer arrived, so he prayed in it.
Then pass by again until you return, so pray by the graves of the martyrs as Allah has decreed for you.
Then proceed on your way until you come to the Mosque of the Confederates (Al-Ahzaab), so pray in it and supplicate to Allah in it.

For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) supplicated in it on the Day of the Confederates and said: 'O Helper of the distressed, and O Responder to the call of the desperate! O Helper of the worried, remove my anxiety, my distress, and my grief, for You see my state and the state of my companions.'

key_terms.قُبَا: Quba (the first mosque built by the Prophet)
key_terms.مَشْرَبَةَ أُمِّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: The drinking place of Umm Ibrahim
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْأَحْزَابِ: The Day of the Confederates (Battle of Khandaq)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended order for visiting mosques and graves around Medina according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes a structured ritual tour (ziyarat) of Medina’s sacred sites, reflecting the Shia emphasis on connecting with the physical history of the Prophet and his family. It details a specific sequence starting with Masjid Quba, moving through the Prophet’s residence and the site of Uhud, and concluding with the Mosque of the Confederates, where the Prophet’s specific supplication for the distressed is preserved. This narrative underscores the theological importance of visiting graves as a means of spiritual reinforcement and remembrance of the Ahl al-Bayt’s trials.
